::: {.callout-note}
## What this is

A single targeted test, not a new analysis of the funnel. It asks one question of the
funnel's largest family-level effect — the enriched Pfam families' +14.6-point excess over
an order-matched null — and answers it by joining the existing cluster tables against NCBI
BioProject metadata.

It is a **companion to [the funnel findings](../delta_gain/)**, which reports that effect in
section 5.1. Read that page's qualification box first if you have not.

The source of truth is
[`analysis/delta_gain_funnel/`](https://github.com/1KFG/delta-gain-fungi/tree/main/analysis/delta_gain_funnel)
in this repository — code, tests, SLURM driver and the per-family output tables that the
numbers below are computed from. This page renders `REPORT.md` from that directory, so the
two cannot drift.

The report is explicit that it does **not** recompute the +14.6-point figure: doing that
needs the order-matched null re-run with the Y1000+ genomes moved into the baseline, which
has not been done. It shows the figure rests on a confound, which is a different claim.
:::
